stages.name: Story and optional missions
stages.text: Play the story at your own pace through all five chapters. Along the way, do the things that count later: the Chapter 1 meditation (see Positive Mental Attitude — the one possibly missable trophy), take optional missions as they appear (100% needs any 100 of them), scan every new vehicle with the WAiNK app (100% needs 200 of 277), and study new animals through the binoculars (100% needs 100 of 255). Turn on progress and criminal profile notifications in the UI settings so you can see what counts. There are no mission medals this time and no mission replay, so keep a manual save at the start and end of each chapter — the game has 15 manual slots plus one autosave.

stages.name: The 100% checklist and challenges
stages.text: The checklist appears after the story, under Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion. Progress made during the story already counts, and nothing on it is missable. PowerPyx calls it lenient — about 60% true completion — but Push Square warns you need almost everything, including 15 of the 18 card sets. Work the checklist in any order: stunts, shooting ranges, drone races, card sets, meditation spots, challenges and robberies. This stage is where most of the remaining trophies pop.

stages.name: Strangers & Freaks and cleanup
stages.text: Most trophies should be done by now. Strangers & Freaks is not part of 100% completion, so finish the eight stranger strands — the five named ones (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) plus any other stranger strands — then sweep up the one-off trophies: the jet at VCIA, the tank at Mile Zero, the jewelry store, the bowling operation, and whatever is left on the list. The platinum follows.

summary: One playthrough, three stages. PowerPyx puts the story at about 60 to 80 hours and the platinum at about 200 hours; Push Square says 250+ hours. Most of that time is the 100% checklist, not the story. Sources: SixShore trophy guide (citing PowerPyx and Push Square).
title: Roadmap to the platinum
